name: AApoAII Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Histological demonstration of amyloid deposits with Congo red staining showing apple-green birefringence
Identification of apolipoprotein A-II as the amyloid fibril protein by immunohistochemistry or mass spectrometry
Presence of clinical manifestations consistent with amyloidosis such as nephrotic syndrome or cardiac involvement
Detection of pathogenic variants in the APOA2 gene associated with amyloidogenicity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of amyloid deposits with apolipoprotein A-II identification is required; clinical features and genetic testing support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires tissue biopsy and specific protein identification due to overlap with other amyloidoses

pathognomonic.symptomName: Renal amyloid deposition causing proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome
searchTerms: protein in urine with kidney damage

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cardiac amyloid infiltration leading to restrictive cardiomyopathy
searchTerms: restrictive heart disease due to amyloid

common.symptomName: Peripheral edema secondary to nephrotic syndrome
searchTerms: swelling in legs from kidney problems
peripheral edema due to nephrotic syndrome
shortness of breath from heart issues
difficulty breathing due to heart involvement
dizziness when standing from nerve damage
orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic neuropathy

common.symptomName: Mild hepatomegaly due to amyloid infiltration
searchTerms: mild hepatomegaly caused by protein deposits

occasional.symptomName: Carpal tunnel syndrome from amyloid deposition in ligaments
searchTerms: wrist nerve compression from ligament deposits
carpal tunnel syndrome from amyloid in ligaments

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous purpura due to vascular amyloid deposits
searchTerms: skin bruising from blood vessel deposits
purple skin spots due to amyloid

rare.symptomName: Gastrointestinal bleeding from amyloid-related mucosal fragility
searchTerms: blood loss from bowel wall fragility

laboratory: Proteinuria with nephrotic range protein loss
Elevated serum creatinine in renal impairment
imaging: Echocardiogram showing restrictive cardiomyopathy with thickened ventricular walls
Renal ultrasound may show normal or enlarged kidneys
MRI with late gadolinium enhancement in cardiac amyloidosis
other: Tissue biopsy with Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Immunohistochemistry or mass spectrometry confirming apolipoprotein A-II as amyloid fibril protein

distinguishingFeatures: Amyloid fibrils composed of serum amyloid A protein
Amyloid fibrils composed of transthyretin protein
Often presents with neuropathy and cardiomyopathy

redFlags: Restrictive cardiomyopathy with heart failure symptoms
Unexplained peripheral neuropathy with autonomic dysfunction
references: Sipe JD, Benson MD, Buxbaum JN, et al. Nomenclature 2014: Amyloid fibril proteins and clinical classification of the amyloidosis. Amyloid. 2014;21(4):221-224.
Obayashi K, et al. AApoAII amyloidosis: a novel form of hereditary systemic amyloidosis. Amyloid. 2013;20(4):234-241.
